newsitem.title: USA: Pipe leak releases asbestos in New York.
newsitem.headline: Pipe leak releases asbestos in New York.

text.p: A leak from an underground steampipe released asbestos into the air Thursday in downtown New York City, forcing more than 20 people to undergo decontamination in case of asbestos exposure, authorities said.
The leak, believed to be from a two-inch service line into an office building, occurred at about 1:20 p.m. just a few blocks from City Hall and the financial district.
Tests showed "asbestos had been released from the steam pipe break," said Consolidated Edison's Mike Spall, a spokesman for the utility company.
Six occupants of the building at 67 Reade St., two passers-by and 15 firefighters were decontaminated at the scene, a spokeswoman for the Department of Environmental Protection said.
The decontamination process involves taking powerful showers with a strong cleansing agent, in specially built mobile trucks, a Fire Department spokesman said.
Inhalation of asbestos fibers can lead to asbestosis, lung cancer and other diseases.
Con Edison shut off steam service to seven buildings nearby, leaving them without heat or hot water, and the block was closed while the asbestos was cleaned up.
